statement: A competition involving $n \geq 2$ players was held over $k$ days. In each day, the players received scores of $1, 2, 3, \ldots, n$ points with no two players receiving the same score. At the end of the $k$ days, each player had exactly $26$ points in total. Determine all pairs $(n, k)$ for which this is possible.

$\dfrac{n(n+1)}{2}$ distinct numbers are arranged at random into $n$ rows, where the $i$-th row has $i$ numbers. Find the probability that the largest number in each row is smaller than the largest number in every row with more numbers.

The feet of the perpendiculars from the intersection point of the diagonals of a convex cyclic quadrilateral to the sides form a quadrilateral $q$. Show that the sum of the lengths of each pair of opposite sides of $q$ is equal.

A particle can travel at speeds up to $2\,\text{m/s}$ along the $x$-axis, and at speeds up to $1\,\text{m/s}$ elsewhere in the plane. Provide a labelled sketch of the region which can be reached within one second by the particle starting at the origin.

The function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfies $f(1) = 1$, $f(2) = 2$, and
$$f(n+2) = f(n+2-f(n+1)) + f(n+1-f(n)).$$
Show that $0 \leq f(n+1) - f(n) \leq 1$. Find all $n$ for which $f(n) = 1025$.
